acceptance_criteria: The workflow count and names are reported from the tree, with the enumeration shown.
Each workflow is driven end to end and its terminal reported verbatim.
Any workflow that cannot be driven provider-free is named, with the node that blocks it.
No workflow, bound, threshold, gate or check was modified — asserted.
The outcome per workflow is recorded in §6 as a measured fact.
Suite count reported before and after.
assumptions: The -051 harness's deterministic client can be configured per workflow. If each needs bespoke stubbing, say so and report the cost rather than building four harnesses.
constraints: FREE. No paid call, no provider, no key. Extend the -051 harness; do not build a second one.
ENUMERATE THE WORKFLOWS BY READING workflows/*.yaml. Do not trust a remembered list or this command's count. Report the count and the names found.

For each workflow: drive it end to end provider-free with a deterministic client that satisfies its gates, and report the terminal verbatim. Per workflow state whether it reached completed, escalated, blocked, or no terminal.
Where a workflow cannot be driven provider-free because a node has no deterministic path, NAME THE NODE that blocks it. That is a testability finding and it is reported, not worked around.
Do NOT fix any defect found. Report it. A defect in a workflow's wiring is a behaviour change and needs a ruling.
Do NOT change any workflow, bound, threshold, gate or check.
Record the outcome per workflow in HANDOVER.md §6 as a measured fact. A workflow that reaches no terminal is recorded as such, plainly, with the node or bound it stopped at.
Keep the diff small. Suite reported before and after.
evidence: HANDOVER.md §3 — the workflow files under workflows/; only engineering-rnd has been driven end to end
.orchestration/responses/ARCH-20260923-051.response.json — the provider-free harness driving engineering-rnd through three criterion outcomes; reuse it
.orchestration/responses/ARCH-20260923-053.response.json — the exhausted terminal names the unmet criteria, so a failure per workflow is legible
.orchestration/responses/ARCH-20260923-054.response.json — the fourth case; recovery reaches a terminal at 28 AI calls
AGENTS.md convention 22 — an instrument's test simulates the condition it watches, end to end
AGENTS.md convention 26 — a report states what it measured and nothing more
objective: Drive all four workflows end to end provider-free and report, per workflow, whether it reaches a terminal — establishing whether the harness works beyond the one pipeline that is proven.

preconditions.expected: The workflow files; record count and names.

questions: If a workflow cannot be driven provider-free at all, is that a testability defect or a deliberate design? Report which the code shows.
Does each workflow share the same graph executor and node kinds, or does one use a construct the others do not? If the latter, name it — that is where the untested surface is.
rollback: Revert the commit; the added cases are removed and the -051 harness is unaffected.
transport: Commit this command file verbatim as carriage before executing; commit the response IN_PROGRESS first, then update it in place. delivery_state must carry the PR number per Ruling D16.

verification.expected: The workflow files enumerated; count and names reported.
Empty — no wiring or check modified by a measurement of it.
